scope: Read-only frontier accounting binding. Design observations, no implementation or service acceptance.

findings.contract: Physical queue identity captures queryId/FI/planNodeId once; future group frontier account must have its own stable key rather than charge each lane for the whole group.

Current path registers MemorySide.OUTPUT then reserveWithPriority on tsBlock.getSizeInBytes; async listener enqueues a pending block under queue monitor; prepaid mode must bypass both registration charge and per-block pool reserve.
Current path frees per-block reservedBytes from pool. Prepaid mode must return internal credit, preserving original group pool reservation while consumer retains a head.
All termination paths free pool bytes. New queue mode must route each to idempotent internal credit settlement before final group free.
Monotone min cap cannot serve as runtime DOP control or as physical prepayment.
Register group account on OUTPUT. Existing account side cannot be rebound.
Needed for FI-side shared cap. tryReserve without sharedBudget enforces plan-local rather than whole-FI cap.
Nonblocking real pool allocation. Check complete batch then rollback already allocated groups on any failure; never count high-priority zero-reservation as successful frontier admission.

next_design_constraints: Use actual retained block bound for new frontier credits, or prove size-in-bytes plus retained overhead is covered elsewhere; current getSizeInBytes accounting alone is not a proof of total physical memory.
Credit path must limit each lane to one queued bounded block and return a pending producer-space future while occupied; remove restores that lane credit without global pool free.
Consumer retained heads, pending producer block and fixed reader state remain in base estimate; releasing queue credit does not free a block still referenced by merge.
Complete external futures on existing notification executor or outside handle/group locks, preserving original queue/source/sink lock discipline.
Controller shrinking workers never shrinks fixed logical queues, hash buckets or aggregate ownership. Memory elasticity only covers admitted incremental worker resources.
Acceptance must use real SharedTsBlockQueue, MemoryPool and two-level TableMergeSortOperator at DOP1 with full/delayed/smaller/empty lanes.
